Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
Comments: No %GNI data; absolute price low but no ITU figure

revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced a clearly authoritative ITU-sourced figure, so this row was moved from the fast (Unknown-confirmation) path to the full verification path rather than confirmed as Unknown. Internet Society Pulse, drawing on ITU ICT price-basket data, reports Angola's low-consumption mobile-broadband basket (2GB, cheapest 3G+ plan) at 1.53% of monthly GNI per capita. This is corroborated by ITU's 'Affordability of ICT services 2023' policy brief, which names Angola as one of only four Least Developed Countries (with Bangladesh, Bhutan and Lao P.D.R.) to meet the Broadband Commission's 2% of GNI per capita affordability target in 2023. Original claim of 'no ITU figure' was incorrect. Value Code recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Affordable, 1-2% of GNI per capita), consistent with the 1.53% figure; the exact sub-1% figure needed for Code 5 could not be confirmed, so no upgrade beyond Code 4 is made.
revised_comments: Angola's entry-level mobile-broadband data basket costs approximately 1.53% of monthly gross national income (GNI) per capita, according to ITU price-basket data. This places Angola among a small group of least-developed countries that meet the UN Broadband Commission's affordability target of under 2% of GNI per capita, reflecting a marked improvement in mobile data affordability in recent years.

Definition: The country's e-government development level based on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This composite index measures online service delivery, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital. Indicates the government's capacity to deliver digital public services.

revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced a clearly authoritative UN source, so this row was moved from the fast (Unknown-confirmation) path to the full verification path rather than confirmed as Unknown. The UN's own EGDI country comparison table for the 2024 E-Government Survey lists Angola with an EGDI of 0.4149, ranked 156th of 193 UN member states, in the Middle EGDI (M3) group. This is independently corroborated by Internet Society Pulse, which reports Angola's 'digital public services rating' (EGDI) as 41.49 on a 0-100 scale — the same figure. Original claim that 'no specific EGDI found' was incorrect; a specific, current, authoritative score exists. Value Code recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (EGDI 0.25-0.49, Middle).
revised_comments: Angola scored 0.4149 on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) in the 2024 UN E-Government Survey, ranking 156th of 193 UN member states and placing it in the Middle EGDI group. This reflects moderate, middle-tier development across online service delivery, telecommunications infrastructure and human capital, the three components underlying the index.
